security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU's HELPER(aes64ks1i) at target/riscv/crypto_helper.c:141, for rnum != 0xA, the implementation applies ror32(temp, 8) BEFORE SubBytes (via aesenc_SB_SR_AK), matching the old/superseded Sail spec that did rotate-then-SubBytes-then-XOR. The corrected Sail spec (aligned with the reference sail-riscv implementation) requires SubBytes first, then logical right shift (>>> 8), then XOR with the round constant. The SubBytes and byte-rotation operations do not commute: the old code produces [S(b0), S(b3), S(b2), S(b1)^rc] while the correct behavior produces [0, S(b3), S(b2), S(b1)^rc] for the 32-bit sub-result, differing in the most significant byte.
security_spec.summary: QEMU aes64ks1i helper computes rotate-then-SubBytes (old spec) instead of SubBytes-then-logical-shift (corrected spec), producing incorrect AES-256 key schedule material for rounds 0-9
